newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BRAZIL DEBT OUTLOOK - Roadshows, rah-rah and risk.
newsitem.headline: BRAZIL DEBT OUTLOOK - Roadshows, rah-rah and risk.

text.p: Central Bank foreign affairs director Gustavo Franco will meet with European investors this week to advertize Brazil's new-and-improved credit-risk profile and drum up support for its unprecedented parallel Eurobond.

Franco, with a fresh credit upgrade from Standard & Poor's Corp in tow, opened a roadshow for the parallel bond on Tuesday in London. Stops in Paris, Vienna and Amsterdam are planned later in the week, the Central Bank said.

The parallel bond, the first of its kind for an emerging market issuer, is expected to have a five-year maturity in three tranches denominated in French francs, Austrian schillings and Dutch guilders. All tranches will carry the same maturity and coupon and be fungible, or redenominated to the euro after the single European currency is introduced in 1999.
"The objective of Brazil is to broaden its investor base and establish an early presence in the euro segment," the Central Bank said in a statement.

Officials have not announced the size of the issue, although sources close to the deal say each tranche will be roughly equivalent to $200 million. Officials hope S&P's credit upgrade of Brazil to BB-minus from B-plus earlier this month will shave a few basis points off its launch price.

IN PRIMARY ACTIVITY, Parana state power firm Copel on Tuesday launched its $150 million eight year bond, putable and callable at five, via Santander Investment and Salomon Brothers. It was expected to price later in the day at between 280-300 bp over U.S. Treasuries.

In secondary trade, Brazilian Eurobond spreads widened by an average five basis points last week despite lower-than -expected U.S. consumer price inflation, which led to a rally in Bradys and U.S. Treasuries.
Brazil debt watchers said there was still too much supply in the market, which would keep investors cautious this week.
"There are still a lot of buyers on the sidelines. We're mostly selling CDs and shorter-dated paper up to a year," said a Eurobond trader in Sao Paulo.

TRADERS SPOTTED FEW CHEAP BUYS in the dollar market, although Ford do Brasil's 9-1/4 percent due 2007 (put 03) looked attractive at 250 basis points over Treasuries. The bond was seen tightening to the 220 bp range. Another factor helping the bond is the fact that Ford's 9-1/8 percent due 2001, now trading at 215 bp over, once traded tighter than Brazil's 8-7/8 percent global due 2001 ZQ4P.
The global is now trading at 190 bp over, a fair price but no bargain, according to players who say they see more value in the Deutsche sector.

Cesp's 9-1/4 percent due 2001 tightened last week to 265 bp over, when swapped to the dollar rate, and traders say there is room to narrow further, noting the bond recently traded as tight as 230 bp over the dollar swap.
Brazil's sovereign eight percent Deutsche bond due 2007 held steady at 300 bp over, when swapped to the dollar. The bond has traded as tight as 260 bp over, traders said.
THE BRADY BOND market was not expected to generate much enthusiasm this week, with no big numbers due out in the United States and little to get excited about locally.

Although a closely-watched civil service reform bill was making its way through the Brazilian Congress and the government was gearing up for the privatization of state mining giant CVRD, traders said they were not holding their breath. They noted delays at the congressional and judicial levels could block progress on both items.

"It's like pulling teeth getting the whole process done. It's all taking much longer than people had expected," said one Brady trader referring to the civil service reform bill. The bill is one of several measures seen essential to slash Brazil's massive budget deficit.

Investors were seen focusing on floating rate bonds like EIs and IDUs which are more stable when the U.S. Treasury market is volatile. Still, some traders said fixed-rate C bonds this week could become attractive at 73-3/4. Cs were trading at 74-1/8, or 499 bp over Treasuries at noon EDT/1600 GMT on Tuesday.
